title: Install the mcpindex gate and watch your first HOLD
meta_description: Install the mcpindex gate, see which MCP hosts it wires, then watch it HOLD a silently changed tool contract before your agent acts. About 4 minutes.
h1: Install the gate and watch your first HOLD
outcome: The gate installed and wired into your MCP hosts, and a live contract change held right in front of you, so you know exactly what a HOLD looks like before it matters.

impatient.label: Skip ahead and watch a contract change get held first

body: The tool your agent trusted on Monday can change on Tuesday, with no version bump your client notices. The gate installs locally, pins the declared contract of each tool you wire it in front of on first sight, and HOLDs a call when that contract silently changes, before your agent acts. It is a contract-diff, not a safety verdict, and it stores no credentials. Here is the whole path, start to finish.

steps.heading: Install the gate
steps.body:
Run this in your terminal. It installs the gate binary and rewrites each MCP host's config so that host's servers launch behind the gate. Free, no account, runs locally.

The two commands differ in two ways. The first (uv) runs `mcpindex-config-wire`, which in a terminal asks whether to join the drift network; the default answer is no. The `install.sh` line also registers a background watcher (a launchd LaunchAgent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux) that wires a newly added server within seconds, and `uninstall.sh` removes it with the wiring. `install.sh` does not ask about drift telemetry: it keeps what you chose before, which on a new machine is off.

To switch servers you have already wired to log-only, where a drift is noted and the call proceeds while a tamper hold and an internal error still stop it, run:

`mcpindex-config-wire wire --repin --proxy-cmd "uvx --from mcpindex-gate mcpindex-proxy --posture monitor"`

`--repin` is what rewrites servers that are already wired; without it they stay on guard. The command follows the latest gate release instead of a pinned version, and servers the watcher wires later start on guard. `mcpindex-config-wire status` counts monitor servers as notify-only, because log-only is not protection.

steps.heading: Restart your host
steps.body: Quit and reopen the host you use (Claude Desktop, Cursor, and so on) so it reloads the gated config. Nothing changes about how you call your tools. The gate sits in the path and stays quiet until a contract drifts.
steps.troubleshoot: If tools stop appearing after the restart, run `mcpindex-config-wire status` to check the wiring, or `uninstall.sh` to un-wire every host config and restore the originals.

steps.heading: Watch a contract change get held
steps.body: Now the part that matters. Pin a tool's contract, apply a change, and watch what the gate does. This runs the real diff logic in your browser (the same mapping the installed gate uses), so there is nothing to fake. Try a breaking change and a benign one:

steps.heading: Read the verdict
steps.body: A HOLD means the live contract differs from what you pinned, so the call is paused before your agent acts. A PROCEED means there was no breaking difference (a benign added-optional field can pass through). The verdict is about what changed, never a claim that the tool is safe.

steps.heading: Find the trace on stderr
steps.body: As the gate works it leaves one quiet line per call on your host's stderr, so you can see it is present without it getting in your way.

steps.heading: If you use the SDK wrapper, bookmark your receipts page
steps.body: The one-command install wires the stdio proxy, and the proxy does not post receipts today, so a wire install sends nothing and this page has no rows for it, even though the weekly summary line still links it; its record is the stderr trace above. If you gate calls through the Python SDK wrapper (wrap()), each gated call posts a credential-blind receipt by default: the verdict and the action, never the arguments or content. On the receipt that decision is logged on the trust axis: a PROCEED shows as ALLOW, a HOLD as DENY, an inconclusive as REVIEW. Your install id is a random token at ~/.mcpindex/install_id (run: cat ~/.mcpindex/install_id), and your page lives at mcpindex.ai/receipts?id=<install-id>. Anyone holding that id can open the page, so treat the link like one you would not post. Set MCPINDEX_RECEIPT_INGEST_ENABLED=0 to send no receipts at all. From gate v0.9.0 the gate also prints a local weekly summary line (calls gated, drift seen, holds) that links the same page; the counters are local-only and nothing about that line is sent anywhere.

deep_link.label: Open your Gate Activity
deep_link.look_for: the tool hash, the verdict (ALLOW, REVIEW, or DENY), and the action, one row per gated call. Paste your install id from ~/.mcpindex/install_id, then bookmark the resulting URL.

faq.q: Do I need an account to install the mcpindex gate?
faq.a: No. The gate installs locally with one command, needs no account, and stores none of your credentials: the host passes each server its environment through the gate's process, which never logs or sends it. An account only matters later if you opt into cloud tiers or higher limits.

faq.q: What does a HOLD from the gate actually mean?
faq.a: A HOLD means the tool's live declared contract differs from what you pinned on first sight, so the gate pauses the call before your agent acts. It is a contract-diff (this changed), not a claim that the tool is safe or unsafe.

faq.q: Will the gate change how I use my tools?
faq.a: No. It sits in the path and stays quiet, leaving one trace line per call on stderr. You only notice it when a tool's contract changes and it holds the call for you to look at.
